answer: A velvet rope is not enough when aliases spread like a vine over a trellis. Each one-hour round starts m=0. A public contract activates a key only if SHA256(encode(round,m,key,nonce)) < floor(2^256/[2^20(m+1)]), then increments m. It rejects stale m and duplicate keys; all memberships expire at round end. Slot k=m+1 needs about 2^20 k hashes, so n simultaneous aliases need at least 2^19 n(n+1) expected hashes. Anyone can verify every hash, counter update and expiry on-chain.
